core_hypothesis: Bacterial-cellulose pellicles produced by kombucha/SCOBY can be converted into retrievable low-density porous sorbent pads or boom inserts for uptake of floating oil, followed by contained mechanical recovery of part of the oil fraction and controlled end-of-life processing of the spent sorbent.

supported: Engineered bacterial-cellulose aerogels are a literature-supported oil-sorbent material class.
Pore-preserving drying and wettability control are key design variables.
Mechanical squeezing/pressing can be evaluated as an oil-recovery step.
not_yet_supported: Raw wet SCOBY is an effective field oil-spill sorbent.
Green-tea-derived SCOBY necessarily absorbs more oil than black-tea-derived SCOBY.
Microwave-treated SCOBY is a safe or superior field sorbent.
Any SCOBY-D0 prototype is ready for real petroleum-spill deployment.

design_principle.key_inversion: The BioPapyrus route intentionally collapses pores for a coherent sheet; the oil-sponge route attempts to preserve pore volume and improve oil-over-water selectivity.

primary_arms.reason: Primary literature reports higher bacterial-cellulose yield than black tea for one tested Kombucha-associated strain; this is a yield hypothesis, not an oil-sorption result.
Common kombucha substrate and direct comparator for the green-tea arm.

feedstock_screen.winner_rule: Select feedstock by the joint outcome of dry BC yield, final dry density, porosity proxy, oil uptake, water uptake, oil/water selectivity, mechanical integrity, reproducibility and cost. Tea identity alone cannot define the winner.

drying_structure_matrix.name: PRESSED_AIR_DRY
drying_structure_matrix.expected_tradeoff: Strong sheet, likely lower uptake because of pore collapse.

drying_structure_matrix.name: AIR_DRY_LOW_COMPACTION
drying_structure_matrix.expected_tradeoff: Simpler process but substantial shrinkage/densification may remain.

drying_structure_matrix.name: FREEZE_DRY_UNMODIFIED
drying_structure_matrix.expected_tradeoff: High pore volume candidate but native bacterial cellulose remains hydrophilic.

drying_structure_matrix.name: FREEZE_DRY_ENVIRONMENTALLY_COMPATIBLE_HYDROPHOBIC
drying_structure_matrix.expected_tradeoff: Closest conceptual match to high-performance BC oil sorbents; requires leachate/ecotoxicity validation before environmental use.

drying_structure_matrix.name: CONTROLLED_CARBONIZED_BC_AEROGEL
drying_structure_matrix.expected_tradeoff: Potentially high oil uptake and hydrophobicity, but requires controlled thermal processing, atmosphere characterization and contaminant analysis.

drying_structure_matrix.name: MICROWAVE_TRANSFORMED_BC
drying_structure_matrix.reason: Uncontrolled microwave heating can cause nonuniform heating, steam generation, charring, arcing, ignition and chemically heterogeneous residues. Visual porosity is not proof of useful aerogel structure.

stage_1_geometry.primary_factorial_cells: 2 tea feeds x 4 non-carbonized drying branches x 5 replicates = 40 primary coupons before geometry duplicates
stage_1_geometry.matching_rule: Use the same consortium, sugar loading, fermentation age window, pellicle maturity definition, wash endpoint, starting wet-mass normalization, drying endpoint and test temperature across matched comparisons.

stage_2_pad.gate: Only fabricate after a stage-1 branch passes uptake, selectivity, retention and integrity gates.

stage_3_module.boundary: Examples are simple mass-balance illustrations. Field crude-oil capacity must be measured and may be substantially lower due to water competition, waves, suspended solids, viscosity, temperature and retrieval losses.

safe_first_pass_test.reason: Allows screening of structure, uptake, selectivity and squeeze recovery without immediately introducing petroleum hazards.
safe_first_pass_test.petroleum_transition_gate: Only after safe-surrogate performance is replicated and appropriate chemical/fire/environmental/waste controls are available.

promotion_gates.G3_RETENTION: At least 80% of absorbed surrogate oil remains after standardized passive draining.
promotion_gates.G4_RETRIEVABILITY: At least 95% dry-equivalent sorbent mass remains retrievable with no hazardous fragmentation.
promotion_gates.G5_RECOVERY: If the closed-loop route is claimed, pressing/draining recovers >= 50% of absorbed surrogate oil.
promotion_gates.G6_BATCH_REPLICATION: Lead branch reproduced in at least two independent SCOBY batches.
promotion_gates.G7_SCALEUP: 100 x 100 mm pad preserves at least 80% of coupon-level g/g performance and remains retrievable.
promotion_gates.G8_PETROLEUM_SIMULATION: Only after G1-G7: controlled petroleum simulation with hydrocarbon analysis and waste plan.
promotion_gates.G9_FIELD: Field use requires ecological leachate testing, contaminant-specific performance, boom/pad retrieval validation, regulatory review and a complete spent-sorbent chain.

features: mechanically robust containment mesh if needed

prohibited: shredding or abandoning spent sorbent in the environment

source_anchors.role: ultralight superhydrophobic bacterial-cellulose aerogel oil sorption and squeeze recyclability
hydrophobic bacterial-cellulose composite aerogel oil/water separation

next_gate: EXECUTE A MATCHED GREEN_TEA VS BLACK_TEA PRODUCTION SCREEN, THEN D0-D3 DRYING SCREEN ON 50 x 50 mm COUPONS; RECORD DRY MASS, DENSITY, OIL UPTAKE, WATER UPTAKE, SELECTIVITY, RETENTION, PRESS RECOVERY AND RETRIEVABILITY; DO NOT PROMOTE MICROWAVE OR PETROLEUM FIELD CLAIMS BEFORE THEIR SEPARATE GATES PASS.
